text: This browser has never seen him.
prefix: This browser has never seen him.

text: It cannot check his face, and it cannot check his SIM card.
prefix: It cannot check his face, and it cannot check his SIM card.

text: So how does a website that knows nothing about this laptop trust that it is really Aziz?

text: First, what a side app cannot do.
prefix: First, what a side app cannot do.

text: A browser cannot run the TAF part, so there is no verdict and no face confirmation.

text: All of that lives only in the master app, the mobile bank.
prefix: All of that lives only in the master app, the mobile bank.

text: So a side app has the password and the bank's own SMS service.
prefix: So a side app has the password and the bank's own SMS service.

text: And it has one more tool, the best one: the master app itself.
prefix: And it has one more tool, the best one: the master app itself.

text: Start with a customer who is new.
prefix: Start with a customer who is new.

text: On the website, a new customer types the phone number.

text: The bank's SMS service sends a one-time code.

text: The customer types the code, then a password, two times.

text: The platform makes a customer at level one, a device record for the browser, and a marketplace app account with one session.
prefix: The platform makes a customer at level one, a device record for the browser, and a marketplace app account with one session.

text: The browser is never a trusted device.
prefix: The browser is never a trusted device.

text: And the new app account is marked not confirmed.

text: It stays so until a TAF check in the mobile bank.

text: Hold on to that mark: the next lesson is about it.

text: Aziz is not new.
prefix: Aziz is not new.

text: He types his number and his password.
prefix: He types his number and his password.

text: The password always comes first.
prefix: The password always comes first.

text: No code goes out, and no request goes anywhere, before the password is correct.
prefix: No code goes out, and no request goes anywhere, before the password is correct.

text: Now the platform looks for a session of Aziz in the master app.
prefix: Now the platform looks for a session of Aziz in the master app.

text: He has one, on his phone.
prefix: He has one, on his phone.

text: So the platform sends no code at all.
prefix: So the platform sends no code at all.

text: It makes an approval request instead, and sends a push signal to the mobile bank.
prefix: It makes an approval request instead, and sends a push signal to the mobile bank.

text: The push carries only the request identifier.

text: The mobile bank pulls the request over its own session, and shows it to Aziz.

text: It shows the marketplace, the browser, the network address, the time, and a warning never to give a code to anyone.

text: Two buttons: Approve, and This was not me.

text: Aziz taps Approve.

text: The laptop session starts, and it gets the level of the session that approved it.

text: Aziz passed MyID long ago, on this trusted phone, so the laptop session is at level two.
prefix: Aziz passed MyID long ago, on this trusted phone, so the laptop session is at level two.

text: That is the only way a side-app session reaches level two: an approval in the master app, from a customer at level two.

text: I think this is the strongest part of the design.

text: The approval travels over a session that the bank already trusts.

text: The code alone is enough, but the session is only at level one.
